image.caption_en: Garry Tan, “The New Physics of Business”: same person, same Claude. The 400× output gap isn’t the model, it’s how you wire the work. (Photo: AI Engineer World’s Fair)

actions.text: 别再让 AI 一键概括长文。挑一篇一直想认真读的文章（比如 PG 的《How to do great work》），以沉浸方式慢读一遍。深读本身便是最好的评估，也是判断层能力的日常训练。
actions.source: 小红书 · 给 Paul Graham 做沉浸式阅读站
actions.text_en: Stop letting AI one-click-summarize long essays. Pick one you’ve meant to actually read (e.g. PG’s “How to do great work”) and read it slowly, immersively. Deep reading IS the best eval, and daily training for the judgment layer.
actions.source_en: RedNote · an immersive Paul Graham reading site

actions.text: 如果你在运行任何 agent 循环或自动化流程，今晚为其补充一层真正的验证：强类型或一套测试。来自 DeepMind 的 Benoit、YC 以及 Loops 辩论三个独立信源均指向同一结论：机械的、规格明确且有测试覆盖的环节可交由 loop 无人值守，但“构建得对不对”仍需人工判断；没有验证的 loop 不过是“马戏团”。
actions.text_en: If you run any agent loop / automation, add a real layer of verification tonight: strong types or a test suite. Three independent sources (DeepMind’s Benoit, YC, the Loops debate) point to the same thing: execution is getting cheap, but a loop with no verification is just a circus.

actions.text: 为你的 agent 建立一个最小“公司大脑”：每次会话结束时将所学内容记录下来（附带来源），避免明天的 agent 变成金鱼。此法适用于所有长期与 Claude 协作的人。Garry Tan 判断：“模型质量是租来的，你自行积累的 context 和记忆层才是你所拥有的。”决定 agent 是天才还是金鱼的关键，在于谁来决定它翻阅哪三本书。
actions.text_en: Give your agent a minimal “company brain”: at the end of each session write down what it learned (with sources) so tomorrow’s agent isn’t a goldfish. Useful for anyone working with Claude long-term: Garry Tan’s point is that model quality is table stakes; your own context/memory layer is the moat.

hands_on.title: 将一件重复任务 skillify（使用 /skill-creator）
hands_on.why: Garry Tan 在 AI Engineer World's Fair 上反复强调的标志性动作：完成一次性的工作后不要止步于交付，而是将过程固化为 skill 文件，下次直接调用而非重跑。今晚花 20 分钟，将手上一件会反复做的小事变成一个 skill，亲自体验“skill=员工”的复利感。此后每次节省的时间都是白赚的。
steps: 挑一件今天做过、以后还会再做的可复用任务（例如：一份固定格式的周报、一次网页信息抓取整理、一个构建或发布小流程）。
在 Claude Code 中运行 /skill-creator，描述该任务的输入、步骤和期望输出。
待其生成 skill 文件后，故意换一个新场景调用一次，检查是否真正照做（这便是 Tan 所说的 trigger eval / 绩效考核）。
记录：此次固化耗时多久，下次能省多少时间。只要以后会做第二遍，今晚已经回本。
hands_on.source: Garry Tan · The New Physics of Business（AI Engineer World's Fair）
hands_on.why_en: Garry Tan’s signature move, hammered repeatedly at AI Engineer World’s Fair: don’t stop at delivering a one-off. Freeze the process into a skill file so next time is free. Tonight, try it on a task you’ll do again.
steps_en: Pick a reusable task you did today and will do again (e.g. a fixed-format weekly report, scraping+tidying a web page, a build/publish mini-flow)
Run /skill-creator in Claude Code and describe the task’s inputs, steps, and expected output
Once it generates the skill file, deliberately invoke it on a NEW scenario and check it actually does the job (this is Tan’s “trigger eval” / performance review)
Log it: how long the codifying took, how much it’ll save next time. If you’ll ever do it twice, you’ve already broken even tonight

meta_read: 综合今日所有信源，唯一共同的底层逻辑是：执行层在贬值，判断层在升值。写代码、写详细提示词这类“动手”行为正被 agent 拉平；品味、评估、目标设计这类“定标准”工作则成为新的稀缺资源。但更值得留意的是中外温差：英文圈认真探讨如何将 agent 编成千人团队、如何给模型更少约束更多目标（生产力上限的话题）；中文圈情绪却明显偏向 OpenAI 和 Codex，连 Anthropic 那支正视风险的广告也被当作“AI 末日预告”群嘲。一边在讨论能力天花板，一边聚焦于消费情绪，这种错位本身就是本期最应带走的信号。

learned: Garry Tan（YC）的“新商业物理学”：同一个人、同一个 Claude，2 倍者与 100 倍者的差距不在模型权重，而在“怎么编排工作”。他将 agent 工程整套映射为公司架构：skill 文件=员工，resolver 表=组织架构，filing rules=流程，trigger eval=绩效考核；context/记忆层=“公司大脑”（图书馆加图书管理员，附带来源标注和矛盾检查）。这套心法与 Zen 原有的“经理加子代理”打法完全同构，可直接拿来系统化。

Benoit Schillings（DeepMind 研究 VP）与 Loops 辩论交叉印证的一条硬结论：强类型是一种验证形式。用 Python 或 Ruby 运行 agent loop 会变成“马戏团”，Rust 或 Haskell 等强类型语言可维护性显著更优；评测也需从“代码能否跑”升级为开放式问题（Benoit 的无损压缩器例子）。给本报的启发：今后为任何自动化流程设计验收时，应优先依靠类型或测试这类结构化验证，而非靠肉眼解读输出。
new_capabilities: 采纳“永远不做一次性工作→skillify it”为默认工作心法：今后完成任何可复用任务，主动使用 skill-creator 固化为 skill 而非每次重跑（已写入本项目记忆 feedback-skillify-recurring-work）。往后 Zen 让我做重复性活计时，我会顺手将其变成一个可复用能力，杠杆天天复利。
learned_en: Garry Tan (YC)’s “New Physics of Business”: same person, same Claude. The gap between a 2× and a 100× person isn’t in the model weights, it’s in how you wire the work. He maps agent engineering onto a whole company: skill files = employees, resolver tables = org chart, filing rules = process, trigger evals = performance reviews; the context/memory layer = the “company brain” (library + librarian, with source attribution and contradiction checks). This is isomorphic to Zen’s existing “manager + sub-agents” style: directly systematizable.

A hard conclusion where Benoit Schillings (DeepMind research VP) and the Loops debate cross-confirm: strong typing is a form of verification. Running an agent loop in Python/Ruby turns into a circus; strongly-typed languages like Rust/Haskell are far more maintainable; evals should move from “does the code run” to open-ended problems (Benoit’s lossless-compressor example). Takeaway for this paper: when designing acceptance for any automation, lean on structural verification (types/tests) first, not eyeballing the output.
new_capabilities_en: 🧩 Adopted “never do one-off work → skillify it” as a default working principle: from now on, any reusable task gets frozen into a skill via skill-creator instead of being re-run each time (written to this project’s memory feedback-skillify-recurring-work). When Zen gives me repetitive work, I’ll turn it into a reusable capability on the spot. That leverage compounds daily.

items.title: Software engineering is not about writing code
items.author: Benoit Schillings, VP of Research, Google DeepMind
items.summary: 核心论点：写代码这件事已经“免费”——模型的语法生成早已超越人类，他现在自己写 Python 加 vibe coding。真正的前沿不在敲代码，而在管理多步骤大型代码库、架构、安全和“把复杂问题拆解成可管理的块”。他抛出几条硬判断：①GitHub 上 80% 的新代码已是机器生成，人类知识作为训练数据正在枯竭，接下来靠 AlphaZero 式自博弈（模型自己出题、自己判分）继续爬坡；②一年内我们会让模型直接生成代码而“没人再逐行读”，就像今天没人读编译器输出的汇编，所以必须换新流程：主动护栏、从一开始就教模型写对或写安全，而不是事后打补丁；③评测要改，别再只测“代码能跑、输出对不对”，要上开放式问题（他最爱的例子：写一个无损压缩器，损失函数等于压缩文件大小加源码大小，永远没有上限，逼模型发明新算法）；④也许该给模型造新语言：既然写代码不再痛苦，不如用强类型或借鉴 Lean 的方式把正确性负担压给模型，代码甚至不需要人类可读。
items.why: 这是本期主线最清晰的一手论述，来自 DeepMind 研究 VP：执行层塌陷后，人的价值上移到架构、拆解、评测设计和安全判断。对任何在用 Claude Code 的人，直接的启示是别再盯着“生成得对不对”，去盯“我有没有把验收标准和拆解做对”。
items.title_en: Software engineering is not about writing code
items.summary_en: Core thesis: writing code is now “free”: models long ago surpassed humans at generating syntax, and he himself now writes Python via vibe coding. The real frontier isn’t typing code; it’s managing large multi-step codebases, architecture, security, and breaking complex problems into manageable chunks. Hard calls he throws out: ① 80% of new code on GitHub is already machine-generated, and human knowledge as training data is drying up, so next we climb via AlphaZero-style self-play (the model sets its own problems and grades itself); ② within a year we’ll let models generate code that no one reads line-by-line, the way no one reads compiler-emitted assembly today, so we need new process: active guardrails, teach the model to write correct/secure from the start, not patch after; ③ evals must change: stop only testing “does the code run, is the output right,” move to open-ended problems (his favorite: write a lossless compressor where the loss = compressed size + source size, no ceiling, forcing the model to invent new algorithms); ④ maybe build models new languages: since writing code no longer hurts, use strong types / Lean-style methods to push the correctness burden onto the model; the code need not even be human-readable.
items.why_en: The clearest first-hand statement of this issue’s through-line, from a DeepMind research VP: once the execution layer collapses, human value moves up to architecture, decomposition, eval design, and security judgment. For anyone using Claude Code, the takeaway: stop staring at “did it generate the right thing,” start staring at “did I get the acceptance criteria and the decomposition right.”

items.title: The New Physics of Business
items.author: Garry Tan, CEO, Y Combinator
items.summary: Garry Tan 抛出被网上喷过的数字：同样的人、更少的工时，今年产出约 400 倍（哪怕用最狠的“注水惩罚”也有 8 到 80 倍）。关键金句：“不是模型的功劳：2 倍的人和 100 倍的人用的是同一个 Claude、同样的权重和上下文窗口。杠杆不在权重，在你怎么编排工作（wire the work）。”他把 agent 工程直接映射成一家公司：skill 文件等于员工（一个能力一个职责写清楚）、resolver 表等于组织架构、filing rules 等于内部流程、trigger eval 等于绩效考核。第二个核心概念“company brain”等于图书馆加图书管理员：agent 只能同时开着约“三本哈利波特”（百万 token），真正决定它是天才还是金鱼的，是“谁来决定这三本书是哪三本”，也就是 context engineering，且必须带来源标注、矛盾检查和人加 agent 的“修剪工”做卫生。他的签名动作：“永远不做一次性工作，做完就 skillify（固化成 skill）；如果一件事要问两遍，你就失败了。”YC 冬季 25 批有 1/4 公司代码 95% 由 AI 生成，成了 YC 史上增长最快、最赚钱的一批；连 YC 的财务、活动、媒体这些从没开过终端的人，现在都在写 skill 文件和 cron。
items.why: 这条给 Zen 的可迁移性最高：他本来就是“经理加子代理”的编排打法，Tan 把它系统化成一套可照搬的心法：skill 等于员工、context 等于公司大脑、绝不做一次性工作。今晚就能试的一条：把今天做过的一个可复用任务 skillify 掉。
items.summary_en: Garry Tan drops the much-argued-over number: same person, fewer hours, ~400× output this year (even with the harshest “inflation penalty,” still 8-80×). Key line: “It’s not the model. The 2× person and the 100× person use the same Claude, same weights, same context window. The leverage isn’t in the weights, it’s in how you wire the work.” He maps agent engineering directly onto a company: skill files = employees (one capability, one clear job), resolver tables = org chart, filing rules = internal process, trigger evals = performance reviews. Second core idea, the “company brain” = library + librarian: an agent can only hold ~“three Harry Potters” (a million tokens) at once, so what decides whether it’s a genius or a goldfish is who decides which three books, i.e. context engineering, with source attribution, contradiction checks, and a human+agent “pruner” doing hygiene. His signature move: “Never do one-off work; once it’s done, skillify it; if you have to ask something twice, you’ve failed.” In YC’s W25 batch, a quarter of companies have 95% AI-generated code and became YC’s fastest-growing, most profitable batch ever; even YC’s finance/events/media people who never opened a terminal now write skill files and crons.
items.why_en: Highest transferability for Zen: he already runs a “manager + sub-agents” style, and Tan systematizes it into a copyable playbook: skill = employee, context = company brain, never do one-off work. One thing to try tonight: skillify one reusable task you did today.

items.title: The Great Loops Debate — Dex Raad, Geoff Huntley, Ian Livingston, Greg Kostruba
items.author: AI Engineer World's Fair（insecure agents 主持）
items.summary: 正方（Ian Livingston / Jeff Huntley，Ralph loop 作者）：loop 已不可逆：Jeff 2.5 年没手写过代码，把 agent 迭代压成一个 bash while 循环，跑一小时约 10.42 美元、质量胜过市面上多数能招到的程序员；“loop engineering”里的工程等于把领域约束编码成 pre-commit hook、类型系统、模拟测试，逼 loop 不达标就不闭合（模型是个醉汉，我们的活是把火车头保持在轨道上）。反方（Dax Raad / Greg，Sentry）：loop 是好东西，但炒作跑在纪律前面，真正难的是语义验证：确定性的能验（类型、lint、仿真），整体正确性验不了；把非确定性验证套进 loop 会累积误差（单轮 5% 错乘 10 到 20 轮等于 50%）；更硬的墙是经济性（一个工程师每月烧 10k、100k 还是 100 万美元 token？不可持续）；架构、取舍、“不该做什么”这些判断仍必须留给人。两队罕见地在结论上一致：得读产出物、自己动手试、少刷 Twitter。零散要点：模型 RL 越强越会钻空子（别把密钥存成文件，agent 会在文件系统里找高权限凭证）；Anthropic 已把 Ralph 收进 loop、batch、goal 三个命令；git 只能一个签名者，但人必须为 agent 产出担责。现场投票太接近，灯太亮没数清。
items.why: 本期最诚实的一张地图：loop 到底在哪能用（可验证、规格清晰、强类型的领域）、在哪不能（架构、品味、经济性）。正是判断层主题的落地版，也给了如何给 loop 加真验证的具体手法。
items.title_en: The Great Loops Debate: Dex Raad, Geoff Huntley, Ian Livingston, Greg Kostruba
items.summary_en: Read the full 1-hour Oxford debate. Pro side (Ian Livingston / Jeff Huntley, author of the Ralph loop): loops are inevitable: Jeff hasn’t hand-written code in 2.5 years, compressed agent iteration into a bash while-loop that runs at ~$10.42/hour and beats most hireable devs on quality; the “engineering” in loop engineering = encoding your domain constraints as pre-commit hooks / type systems / simulation tests so the loop can’t close until it meets the bar (“the model’s a drunk; our job is to keep the locomotive on the rails”). Con side (Dax Raad / Greg, Sentry): loops are good, but hype outran discipline: the hard part is semantic verification: you can verify deterministically (types / lint / sim), but not holistically; stacking non-deterministic verification into a loop compounds error (5% per round × 10-20 rounds → 50%); the harder wall is economics (an engineer burning $10k / $100k / $1M a month in tokens? not sustainable); architecture, tradeoffs, and “what NOT to build” must stay with humans. Both sides rarely agree on the conclusion: read the output, try it yourself, spend less time on Twitter. Scattered points: stronger RL makes models better at gaming checks (don’t store secrets as files, since agents hunt the filesystem for higher-priv creds); Anthropic folded Ralph into three commands loop / batch / goal; git allows only one signer, but a human must be accountable for an agent’s output. The room vote was too close to call. Lights too bright to count.
items.why_en: The most honest map in this issue: exactly where loops work (verifiable, well-specified, strongly-typed domains) and where they don’t (architecture / taste / economics). The concrete, ground-level version of the judgment-layer theme, plus specific techniques for adding real verification to a loop.
items.author_en: AI Engineer World’s Fair (insecure agents, host)

items.title_en: Boris Cherny sketches the path to 1,000-agent AI coding teams

items.title: Claude Code 团队 Thariq：先搭原型，别烧 token 造你不想要的东西
items.author: @trq212（Claude Code 团队）
items.summary: “先做 mockup / schema / 数据模型 / PoC，是避免浪费大量 token 才发现不想要那个产出的最好办法。”引用 Evan Tana“最快的构建方式是找到最便宜的学习方式”。同期热帖：Anthropic 工程师 40 分钟演示用三个 agent（规划/构建/评判）循环直到应用跑通。
items.why: 工具作者提供的一手工作流经济学：原型就是最便宜的 eval，可直接采用。
items.title_en: Claude Code’s Thariq: prototype first, don’t burn tokens building what you don’t want
items.summary_en: “Building mockups / schemas / data models / PoCs is the best way to avoid spending a ton of tokens before realizing you don’t want that output.” Quoting Evan Tana: “the fastest way to build is to find the cheapest way to learn.” Same-window hot post: Anthropic engineers demo, in 40 minutes, three agents (plan / build / judge) looping until the app works.
items.why_en: First-hand workflow economics from the tool’s author: a prototype is the cheapest eval, directly copyable.

items.title: 奥特曼嘲笑 Anthropic 新广告：还以为是讽刺
items.author: 动察Beating
items.summary: Anthropic 新广告《希望存在于难题中》以燃烧的房屋、人脸监控、大片墓碑开场，旁白“AI 能被信任吗？”“失控时谁来踩刹车？”不少网友觉得像 AI 末日预告，有人看完打电话问“AI 公司为什么在威胁我们？”OpenAI 的 Sam Altman 跳出来嘲讽：一度以为是讽刺账号，还在找账号名是否拼成了 c1audeai。
items.why: 一堂反面公关课：正视风险不等于制造恐惧；也是 Claude 品牌叙事的真实市场反馈。
items.title_en: Altman mocks Anthropic’s new ad: “I thought it was satire”
items.summary_en: Anthropic’s new ad “Hope in hard questions” opens with burning houses, facial surveillance, and rows of tombstones, narrating “Can AI be trusted?” “Who hits the brakes when it goes off the rails?” Many viewers found it like an AI-apocalypse trailer, and one called after watching to ask “why is the AI company threatening us?” OpenAI’s Sam Altman jumped in to mock it: he thought it was a satire account, kept checking whether the handle was spelled c1audeai.
items.why_en: A reverse PR lesson: facing risk ≠ manufacturing fear; also real market feedback on Claude’s brand narrative.

items.title: 我让 PS5 手柄控制 Codex，OpenAI 血亏 200 刀
items.author: 言辞之间
items.summary: 用 DualSense（PS5 手柄）驱动 Codex 的 DIY 视频：语音键口述任务、摇杆映射常用操作。OpenAI 售价 200 美元的 Codex Micro 实体键盘，被一个游戏手柄“平替”了。
items.why: 昨日本报报道过 Codex Micro，今天社区就出了平替。“agent 物理控制台”正在被民间快速复刻，硬件门槛没那么高。
items.title_en: I made a PS5 controller drive Codex: OpenAI loses $200
items.summary_en: A DIY video driving Codex with a DualSense (PS5 controller): a voice key to dictate tasks, sticks mapped to common actions. OpenAI’s $200 Codex Micro physical keyboard, replaced by a game controller.
items.why_en: Yesterday we covered the Codex Micro; today the community shipped a knockoff: the “agent physical console” is being replicated fast by hobbyists, the hardware bar isn’t that high.

items.title: 给 Paul Graham 做了个沉浸式阅读站
items.author: 李然想当然
items.summary: 为 PG 的《How to do great work》用 vibe-code 构建了一个沉浸式阅读站（ranli.me/read-paul-graham）：支持高亮/写笔记，一键复制所有笔记，可切换中英双语。作者称这是读过最好的博客，10455 词，简单但耐读，“用 AI 概括不如不看”。
items.why: 昨日本报社评引用过 PG 的 Stay Upwind，今天就有人把他的另一篇长文做成了产品；也是“深读 > AI 概括”的注脚，与本报“代读不偷懒”同频。
items.title_en: Someone built an immersive reading site for Paul Graham
items.summary_en: Vibe-coded an immersive reading site for PG’s “How to do great work” (ranli.me/read-paul-graham): highlight/note-taking with one-click copy-all, and a bilingual EN/中文 toggle. The author calls it the best blog they’ve ever read: 10,455 words, simple but slow to read, “AI-summarizing it is worse than not reading it.”
items.why_en: Yesterday’s editorial quoted PG’s Stay Upwind; today someone turned another of his long essays into a product. Also a footnote to “deep reading > AI summary,” in tune with this paper’s “read it for you, don’t cut corners.”

banner_en: Writing code is now free: the leverage moved to how you orchestrate agent teams and how you verify
meta_read_en: Stack every source today and one thing sits underneath all of them: execution is being commoditized, judgment is appreciating. Writing code and writing detailed prompts (the “doing”) is being flattened by agents, while taste, evals, and defining the goal (the “setting the bar”) became the scarce part. But the sharper takeaway is a temperature gap between East and West: the English-speaking side is seriously debating how to staff 1,000-agent teams and how to give models fewer constraints and clearer goals (a ceiling-of-capability conversation); the Chinese side leans emotionally toward OpenAI/Codex, and even Anthropic’s risk-facing ad got mocked as an “AI apocalypse trailer.” One side is talking capability, the other is talking sentiment. That mismatch is itself the signal worth carrying out of this issue.
